cards.title: 谷歌调整 K-12 教育 AI 政策：Gemini、搜索等服务默认关闭
cards.summary: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，当地时间 11 月 3 日，谷歌宣布将从 2027 年起调整面向 K-12（幼儿园至高中）教育用户的人工智能功能管理政策，学校管理员需要主动启用，学生账户才能使用 Gemini、NotebookLM、Gemini in Classroom 以及 Google Search 等相关服务。 谷歌同时明确表示，如果学校选择全面禁用 AI，学生也将无法继续使用 Google Search。 根据谷歌官方公告，该公司将在与学校、教师、研究人员及政策制定者沟通后，调整教育产品的管理方式。新政策实施后，学校管理的 K-12 学生账户中，Gemini、Gemini Notebook、Gemini in Classro…
fulltext: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，当地时间 11 月 3 日，谷歌宣布将从 2027 年起调整面向 K-12（幼儿园至高中）教育用户的人工智能功能管理政策，学校管理员需要主动启用，学生账户才能使用 Gemini、NotebookLM、Gemini in Classroom 以及 Google Search 等相关服务。
谷歌同时明确表示，如果学校选择全面禁用 AI，学生也将无法继续使用 Google Search。
根据谷歌官方公告，该公司将在与学校、教师、研究人员及政策制定者沟通后，调整教育产品的管理方式。新政策实施后，学校管理的 K-12 学生账户中，Gemini、Gemini Notebook、Gemini in Classroom 和 Google Search 将默认关闭，只有学校管理员主动授权后才能使用。谷歌表示，此举旨在让学校自行决定人工智能工具在课堂中的使用方式。
不过，这项政策也意味着学校无法在完全禁用 AI 的同时保留传统搜索服务。Google 教育业务副总裁兼总经理 Chris Phillips 在接受《纽约时报》采访时表示，搜索与人工智能已经深度融合。如果学校选择彻底关闭 AI 功能，学生将无法访问 Google Search，尝试使用搜索服务时，只会看到由学校提供的停用提示信息。
据科技媒体 TechCrunch 报道，学校目前无法单独关闭 Google Search 中的 AI 功能，同时保留传统搜索服务。对于希望学生继续通过搜索引擎查找资料、比较信息来源，但不希望他们接触 AI Overview 等生成式 AI 功能的教育机构而言，这意味着需要在两者之间作出选择。
谷歌此次调整还涉及 AI 辅助学习功能 Guided Learning（IT之家注：该功能旨在通过提问、分步骤解释和互动练习，引导学生自行理解问题，而不是直接提供答案）。谷歌已宣布将 Guided Learning 引入 Google Classroom，并计划将相关能力整合到面向学生账户的 Google Search 中。
谷歌表示，Guided Learning 将首先在美国部分学校开展试点，收集教师反馈后再逐步扩大覆盖范围。按照官方公告，该公司希望通过这一功能，让 AI 在课堂中承担辅助学习的角色。
在此之前，部分教育机构和家长对 AI 工具可能影响学生独立思考、作业完成方式及学习过程表达了担忧。谷歌此次将相关工具调整为默认关闭，需要学校主动启用，但搜索服务与 AI 功能之间的绑定也引发了新的讨论。

cards.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
cards.title_cn: Anthropic正在开发一个系统来证明人工智能模型的身份
cards.summary: 【Anthropic】Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.

Anthropic is working on an open-source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” – a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using.

Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.

FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model. “A developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model,” the researchers write. “How can a user verify these claims?”

To work, the system requires AI labs to publish a “fingerprint” of each model they release that can later be matched to specific outputs and verified cryptographically. Crucially, the fingerprints don’t reveal a model’s weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private. That means labs could publish the fingerprints without giving up their most valuable asset, enabling the system to work with commercial models, too. The system is also designed to be lightweight, so verification could be performed on a local device.

As part of the announcement, researchers released a detailed technical specification and working code for various elements of the system, which is publicly available under an open-source license on GitHub. Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab.

“This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda,” researchers explain in the announcement post. “We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.”

根据周二发布的一篇博客文章， Anthropic正在开发一个开源系统，以验证哪个人工智能模型产生了给定的输出。这个名为FlashProve的系统旨在提供研究人员所谓的“可证明推理” --一种加密证明，本质上是一种数学保证，即给定的输出来自特定模型。它旨在让用户确认他们收到的答案确实来自他们认为他们正在使用的模型。
类似于让收件人确认消息确实来自其声称的发件人的加密电子邮件签名， FlashProve将能够抵御试图将一个模型伪装成另一个模型的冒名顶替者，即使冒名顶替者是构建和运行模型的实验室。研究人员特别指出，该系统可用于防止人工智能公司秘密交换更便宜的模型以削减成本，或更昂贵的模型以夸大其性能结果。
FlashProve还可用于验证第三方声称特定任务是由高级模型完成的。研究人员写道： “开发人员可能会声称他们的软件库是通过前沿网络安全模型扫描漏洞的，或者公司可能会声称其商业计划得到了适当模型的批准。”「用户如何验证这些声明？」
为了工作，该系统要求人工智能实验室发布他们发布的每个模型的“指纹” ，这些模型随后可以与特定输出匹配并进行加密验证。至关重要的是，指纹不会显示模型的权重，定义其行为方式的内部数字，以及Anthropic和OpenAI等封闭模型制造商保持私密的内部数字。这意味着实验室可以在不放弃最有价值资产的情况下发布指纹，从而使系统也能与商业模型配合使用。该系统还设计为轻量级，因此可以在本地设备上进行验证。
作为公告的一部分，研究人员发布了系统各个元素的详细技术规范和工作代码，这些规范和工作代码在GitHub上的开源许可证下公开提供。该系统的研究正在进行中，没有计划在Anthropic或任何其他实验室部署它。
研究人员在公告帖子中解释说： “这篇研究帖子旨在分享中期进展，而不是完整的研究议程。” “我们明确分享这一点，让其他人看看我们做了什么，接受它，并加以改进。”

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，当地时间 11 月 2 日 OpenAI 消费者产品负责人 Adam Fry 在纽约举行的一场 OpenAI 活动期间接受了 Big Technology 的采访。他透露，ChatGPT 每周活跃用户数量已经达到 12 亿之高。
Fry 表示，ChatGPT 的用户增长速度正在进一步加快。过去 60 天内，ChatGPT 的周活跃用户从 10 亿增长至 12 亿，新增约 2 亿用户。他将这一增长速度概括为每 30 天增加约 1 亿用户。
搜索业务方面，Fry 透露，OpenAI 对 ChatGPT 内部的搜索类查询进行了统计，并与 Google 的搜索查询量进行比较，结果显示，ChatGPT 当前处理的搜索类查询量约为 Google 的五分之一，每周生成图片达到 15 亿张，语音输入和语音对话功能的合计周活跃用户达到 2.5 亿。
Fry 解释称，只要用户提出的问题触发了 ChatGPT 的联网搜索，就会被计为一次搜索。相关查询包括人物、地点、事物的信息检索，以及需要获取最新信息的金融、健康等问题。单纯的写作和编程请求则不属于这一统计范畴。
Fry 还提到，ChatGPT 的语音输入和语音对话功能合计拥有 2.5 亿周活跃用户，每周生成的图片数量达到 15 亿张。这表明语音交互和图像生成也已经成为 ChatGPT 的重要使用场景。

cards.title: Google is entirely disabling Search in schools that don’t want AI
cards.title_cn: 在不需要人工智能的学校中，谷歌将完全禁用搜索功能
cards.summary: 【Google】Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times. The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on T…
fulltext: Students in schools that reject Google’s AI will see notices that Search isn’t available.

Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times. The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search “will be entirely off” for K-12 student accounts unless “administrators explicitly turn them on.”

Administrators will not be given the option to toggle Gemini-powered features off without disabling Search, however. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the NYT, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” adding that schools that disable Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” Google didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

The announcement comes just months after Google turned its Gemini AI assistant on by default inside the Google Classroom app, which is used by more than 150 million teachers and students globally. The move added to skepticism surrounding Google’s introduction of AI in schools amid reports of declining test scores and other impacts on students’ learning abilities. Last month, lawmakers pressed Google on the “potential harms” of putting its AI products in schools. Although Google is no longer turning on AI features in schools by default, this choice comes at a cost.

Several lawmakers and local leaders have responded to Google’s move to block Search, with Sen. Bernie Sanders (D-VT) calling it “extortion” and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani saying, “no corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.” Rohit Chopra, California’s Secretary of Business & Consumer Services, wrote that Big Tech shouldn’t be able to “strong-arm schools.”
Google argues that this change will “give schools more choice, not less,” adding that schools can choose to turn off each service on or off individually.

The company is also attempting to address concerns about students using its AI features to find “shortcuts” instead of solving problems themselves. Google is embedding its Guided Learning feature, which is supposed to help students work through problems, into its AI Overviews in Search. Google will begin testing this feature in select US schools this month.
Update, November 3rd: Added responses from lawmakers and Google.

cards.summary_cn: 【Google】谷歌告诉《纽约时报》，该公司正在完全关闭拒绝其人工智能功能的学校的搜索功能。谷歌在更广泛的教育相关更新中也分享了这一决定。
fulltext_cn: 拒绝谷歌人工智能的学校的学生将看到搜索不可用的通知。
谷歌告诉《纽约时报》，该公司正在完全关闭拒绝其人工智能功能的学校的搜索功能。周二，谷歌在更广泛的教育相关更新中也分享了这一决定，称除非“管理员明确开启” ，否则对K-12学生帐户的Gemini、Gemini Notebook、Gemini in Classroom和Google Search的访问权限将“完全关闭”。
但是，管理员将无法在不禁用搜索的情况下切换双子座功能。谷歌教育副总裁克里斯·菲利普斯（ Chris Phillips ）告诉纽约时报， “搜索和人工智能是深度融合的” ，并补充说，禁用谷歌人工智能功能的学校“将无法访问搜索，他们将看到来自学校的消息，表明它不可用。“谷歌没有立即回复The Verge的评论请求。
就在几个月前，谷歌在Google Classroom应用程序中默认开启了Gemini AI助手，全球有超过1.5亿教师和学生使用该应用程序。此举加剧了对谷歌在学校引入人工智能的怀疑，因为有报道称考试成绩下降以及对学生学习能力的其他影响。上个月，立法者向谷歌施压，要求将其人工智能产品投入学校的“潜在危害”。尽管谷歌不再默认在学校中启用人工智能功能，但这种选择是有代价的。
一些立法者和地方领导人对谷歌阻止搜索的举动做出了回应，参议员伯尼·桑德斯（民主党-佛蒙特州）称之为“敲诈勒索” ，纽约市市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼（ Zohran Mamdani ）说： “任何公司都不应该有权决定我们如何教育我们的孩子。加利福尼亚州商业和消费者服务部长罗希特·乔普拉（ Rohit Chopra ）写道，大型科技公司不应该拥有“强大的学校”。
谷歌认为，这一变化将“给学校更多的选择，而不是更少的选择” ，并补充说，学校可以选择单独关闭每项服务。
该公司还试图解决学生使用其人工智能功能寻找“捷径”而不是自己解决问题的担忧。谷歌正在其AI Overviews in Search中嵌入其引导式学习功能，该功能旨在帮助学生解决问题。谷歌将于本月在美国部分学校开始测试此功能。
更新， 11月3日：添加了立法者和Google的回复。

fulltext: IT之家 11 月 4 日消息，苹果公司今天推送 macOS 27.3 Golden Gate 首个开发者测试版，内部版本号为 26C5035r，距离上周推出 macOS 27.2 仅约一周。
科技媒体 9to5Mac 称本次更新主要亮点在于扩展 Siri AI 语言支持，不过目前该信息依然有待验证。苹果 Siri AI 上线初期仅支持英语，在 macOS 27.2 更新中上线法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语。
苹果公司此前承诺在 2026 年年底之前，在上述语言支持基础上，再扩展支持繁体中文、挪威语、土耳其语以及越南语。上述语言支持可能已在 macOS 27.3 Golden Gate 首个开发者测试版中上线，并于 12 月随 macOS 27.3 正式版上线普及。
此外针对国行 Apple 智能，苹果公司今天已通过 iOS 27.3 首个开发者预览版更新，解锁首批 Apple 智能技能，但首批仅面向 iPhone，而 Mac 等其他平台依然需要等待一段时间。
macOS 27.3 可能延续上一版本引入的手势识别工具，进一步调整系统底层和界面，以适配触控输入。
苹果公司还发布了 macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 和 macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 的首个候选版本，继续支持旧版 macOS。macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 的发布版本号为 24H314，而 macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 的发布版本号为 25G416。

cards.title: Google is making it harder for schools to say no to AI (Update: Statement)
cards.title_cn: 谷歌让学校更难对人工智能说不（更新：声明）
cards.summary: 【Google】Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR Google plans to turn off AI tools in its software for K-12 students next year, unless school administrators explicitly turn them on. At the same time,…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.
Update: November 3, 2026 (3:59 PM ET): Google has provided a statement, clarifying its announcement regarding AI controls for K-12 students.

Original article: November 3, 2026 (2:13 PM ET): From Help me write to quiz generation, Google has packed its products full of AI tools that could help students along their academic journey. At the same time, these tools can easily be used as shortcuts, preventing students from truly learning from their lessons. Even Google understands why there’s skepticism around the use of AI in education. As such, the company is turning off access to these tools in its software for K-12 students, but it will come at a cost.

While announcing Guided Learning integration in Google Search and Google Classroom, the tech giant revealed that it is updating its approach to controls for its AI products. Early next year, access to tools like Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and more will be disabled for K-12 student accounts. School administrators will need to explicitly turn these tools on for students to have access.

Google states that it made this decision after listening to feedback from schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers. However, the decision is a bit of a double-edged sword. Schools that choose to restrict access to Google’s AI tools will also lose access to Search.

“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” VP for Education at Google Chris Phillips explained to The New York Times. So if a school refuses to allow access to AI, students “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

Google Search is such a dominant force in the search engine landscape that it’s become synonymous with the act of looking up information online. Losing access to the internet’s most preferred search tool would be a big loss for any school, which could lead to schools reluctantly agreeing to the tech giant’s conditions. It just highlights how powerful Google has become in the education sector.

原文： 2026年11月3日（美国东部时间下午2:13 ） ：从帮助我写作到测验生成，谷歌的产品中充满了人工智能工具，可以帮助学生完成学业。同时，这些工具可以很容易地用作快捷方式，防止学生真正从课程中学习。甚至谷歌也明白为什么人们对人工智能在教育中的使用持怀疑态度。因此，该公司正在关闭其K-12学生软件中对这些工具的访问权限，但这需要付出代价。
在宣布将引导式学习集成到谷歌搜索和谷歌课堂的同时，这家科技巨头透露，它正在更新其人工智能产品的控制方法。明年初， K-12学生帐户将禁用Gemini、Gemini Notebook等工具。学校管理人员需要明确开启这些工具，以便学生获得访问权限。
谷歌表示，它是在听取了学校、教师、主要研究人员和政策制定者的反馈意见后做出这一决定的。不过，这个决定有点双刃剑。选择限制访问谷歌人工智能工具的学校也将失去对搜索的访问权限。
“搜索和人工智能深度融合，”谷歌教育副总裁克里斯·菲利普斯（ Chris Phillips ）向《纽约时报》解释道。因此，如果学校拒绝允许访问人工智能，学生“将无法访问搜索，他们将看到来自学校的消息，表明它不可用。”
Google搜索在搜索引擎领域占据主导地位，已成为在线查找信息的代名词。失去互联网上最受欢迎的搜索工具对任何学校来说都是一大损失，这可能导致学校不情愿地同意这家科技巨头的条件。它只是突出了谷歌在教育领域的强大地位。

cards.title: One of Android’s biggest software rollouts is here, with over 80 devices on the guest list
cards.title_cn: 安卓最大的软件发布之一即将推出，宾客名单上有80多台设备
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】TL;DR Xiaomi has revealed its global HyperOS 4 rollout roadmap, covering 80+ phones and tablets across three waves. The rollout begins in early November, expands in mid-November, and reaches more devi…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Apple may have trademarked the art of making glass look exciting on phones, but Xiaomi clearly didn’t get the memo about keeping a safe distance. After borrowing a page from Apple’s design playbook with its translucent HyperOS 4 interface, the Chinese manufacturer is ready to put its latest software makeover in millions of hands. This time, there’s a proper global rollout calendar to go with the shiny new coat of paint.

Xiaomi has published its global HyperOS 4 rollout schedule, confirming that the stable update will begin reaching eligible Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO devices this November, with more joining through December. The announcement follows September’s global beta program, which initially targeted a handful of flagships. Now, the guest list has expanded considerably, covering 82 phones and tablets across three rollout waves.
Xiaomi has divided the global rollout into three waves, with the first devices scheduled to receive the update in early November.
These are rollout starting windows rather than guaranteed installation dates, so availability may vary by device and region.

As for what’s arriving, HyperOS 4 introduces Xiaomi’s Soft Light Glass design, complete with translucent panels, layered notifications, redesigned lock screens, and more customization options. The update also introduces performance improvements and smarter device management.

Apple’s Liquid Glass influence is hard to miss, although Xiaomi isn’t exactly breaking new ground with the look. Even OPPO is doing the same with ColorOS 17, and Google has also been embracing similar translucent effects in Android 17.

Speaking of Android 17, HyperOS 4 is based on both Google’s latest OS and the previous Android 16, with some devices having received Android 17 with HyperOS 3. For those phones, the real attraction is Xiaomi’s own collection of visual and functional upgrades.
Still, beneath all that borrowed sparkle is a substantial software upgrade. And for owners of older Xiaomi phones, the most exciting part might be seeing their devices make the cut.

cards.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
cards.title_cn: StateBench ：测试语言模型如何跟踪长文档的状态变化
cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
fulltext: 📄 Tech Report | 🤗 Data | 💻 Code
We’re introducing StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking—how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.

State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed. However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer. For example, a harder variant of our mystery state tracking would be if John gave Mary the item in his backpack, with it previously known that Edward put a knife in John’s backpack.

Transformers have well-documented theoretical limits on hard variants of state tracking with long dependency chains, helping motivate recurrent and hybrid architectures such as Gated DeltaNet that carry a running memory forward. Existing state-tracking tests tend to focus on the hardest cases, but as these designs become more common, researchers need to know which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle. We would like to understand the differences between architectures not just on the hardest kinds of state tracking, but also on the simpler, potentially more common kinds.

To this end, we developed the StateBench benchmark to capture state-tracking problems of different complexity, which we used to evaluate the differences between language models with different architectures. We find that recurrent and hybrid models can generalize much farther than transformers when trained directly on these tasks, while frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer.

StateBench consists of four difficulty levels that permit increasingly complex state update operations. For programmers, these levels of state tracking complexity can be understood as allowing different types of variable assignment operations:

These levels can be intuitively understood in terms of variable assignments, but they also represent theoretically motivated distinctions in state tracking rooted in Krohn–Rhodes theory, a branch of algebra that describes how state-tracking problems – which can be viewed as word problems over finite monoids – can be decomposed into atomic primitives. Each level in our hierarchy corresponds to a class of state-tracking problems that can be built out of a different set of primitives.

To compare the four levels fairly, we start with a general finite sequence of variable assignments and derive three easier versions from it, producing four comparable StateBench problems—one at each difficulty level. All four use the same number of variables and distinct values, with assignments appearing at the same points in the sequence; only the type of assignment changes.

We tested a range of open pretrained models on the r-trivial, aperiodic, and general finite levels of StateBench to see where their state tracking breaks down, and whether different architectures fail where theory predicts. Under standard theoretical assumptions, transformers can handle r-trivial robustly (and soluble and aperiodic to some degree) but are predicted to fail on general problems. In contrast, Gated DeltaNet with a more flexible memory update can, in principle, handle all four levels.

We started with open pretrained models, where the training data and context lengths are fully documented. These included two 7-billion-parameter models, Olmo 3 (a transformer) and Olmo Hybrid (which adds Gated DeltaNet layers), along with smaller models with 275 million and 2.7 billion parameters. All of these models were pretrained on the same data; none had seen contexts longer than 64,000 tokens during training, and we tested most of them on inputs well beyond that length.

When we scored each model, almost all performed well on r-trivial problems, lost accuracy on aperiodic ones as inputs grew, and stayed at chance on general finite problems. Problem format mattered here—the 275-million-parameter hybrid and Gated DeltaNet models scored near the ceiling on RULER-style r-trivial problems but were near chance on the same problems framed as spreadsheet edits. That gap is one reason StateBench tests the same underlying problem in several formats.

We then tested four frontier models – Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna – asking them to read each sequence of variable assignments and generate the final value of every variable.

All four performed well on r-trivial and aperiodic problems. But on soluble and general finite problems, accuracy fell sharply as inputs grew longer, dropping to 13% or lower on the longest general finite problems. One likely factor is sensitivity; at these harder levels, many more steps can affect the final answer, leaving less room for a model to miss an update without getting the result wrong.

Next, we investigated whether models’ difficulty with the harder levels reflects limits of the architectures themselves, or whether pretraining simply doesn’t teach models to solve them. Targeted direct training is a more favorable setting that reveals to what degree state-tracking issues come from the underlying architecture and optimizer rather than the data used to pretrain a model.

We trained several 275-million-parameter models from scratch on StateBench: two transformer variants, two hybrids, and two Gated DeltaNet variants with different memory-update constraints. The models trained on sequences of up to 256 assignments and were tested on sequences as long as 64,000 assignments, or 250 times the maximum training length.

The architectures began to diverge as sequences grew longer. Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models generalized almost perfectly on r-trivial, aperiodic, and soluble problems out to the longest sequences we tested, tens of thousands of assignments. Transformers learned the easier levels but degraded on longer sequences, and they never learned general finite problems. On the hardest level, the Gated DeltaNet variant with a more flexible memory update generalized the farthest, staying near perfect out to roughly 10 times the length of the longest sequences it saw during training.

For Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models, the gap points to training rather than architecture; trained directly, they learned to handle state-tracking levels their pretrained counterparts couldn’t. Transformers were different—even trained directly, they could never learn the hardest level.

Some questions remain open. Our new proof shows that Gated DeltaNet with a more limited memory update (non-negative eigenvalues) can solve all aperiodic tasks and certain periodic tasks, such as tracking whether a repeated input has occurred an even or odd number of times, under the paper’s fixed-precision arithmetic with rounding. Its exact placement in the hierarchy remains open, including whether it can solve all soluble tasks and how numerical precision or combining it with attention layers affects its capabilities. StateBench also assumes a fixed number of variables, while real tasks often introduce new entities over time. In a long conversation, for example, new people and objects can appear as it unfolds, and the model has to begin tracking them too. The current framework doesn’t yet cover that setting.

As new flavors of recurrent and hybrid architectures emerge, understanding which kinds of state tracking each can handle could help guide how future systems are developed and trained. We hope StateBench gives researchers a finer-grained way to find where models break down—and to build training and evaluation data for the capabilities that still fall short. More fundamentally, we hope it serves as a North Star for researchers to develop new architectures with more robust state-tracking abilities compared to current models.

cards.summary_cn: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】StateBench ：测试语言模型如何跟踪长文档的状态变化
fulltext_cn: 📄 技术报告|🤗数据| 💻代码
我们正在引入StateBench ，这是一种长上下文状态跟踪的基准测试-语言模型如何在长文档中跟踪有关实体的信息。

状态跟踪是任务的基础，从读取代码（分配和重新分配变量）到跟踪故事（角色实际移动和对象易手）。例如，如果一部神秘小说在谋杀发生前说“约翰给了玛丽刀” ，那么重要的是要知道每个角色的状态都发生了变化。然而，并非所有的状态跟踪问题都是相同的：有些问题只需要找到最新的更新；较难的问题需要遵循一系列更改，其中一个错过的步骤可能会丢弃最终答案。例如，我们的神秘状态跟踪的一个更难的变体是，如果约翰把背包里的物品交给玛丽，以前就知道爱德华在约翰的背包里放了一把刀。
变压器对具有长依赖链的状态跟踪的硬变体具有有据可查的理论限制，有助于激励递归和混合架构，例如承载运行内存的门控DeltaNet。现有的状态跟踪测试往往侧重于最困难的情况，但随着这些设计变得越来越普遍，研究人员需要知道每个架构可以处理哪种状态跟踪。我们希望了解架构之间的差异，不仅在最难的状态跟踪类型上，而且在更简单、可能更常见的类型上。
为此，我们开发了StateBench基准来捕获不同复杂性的状态跟踪问题，我们使用该基准来评估具有不同架构的语言模型之间的差异。我们发现，当直接对这些任务进行训练时，循环模型和混合模型可以比变压器泛化得更远，而包括Gemini 3.8 Flash、Claude Opus 5.5和GPT-6 Sol和Luna在内的前沿模型仍然会随着输入的增长而分解更难的状态跟踪形式。
StateBench由四个难度级别组成，允许越来越复杂的状态更新操作。对于程序员来说，这些级别的状态跟踪复杂性可以理解为允许不同类型的变量赋值操作：
这些级别可以通过变量赋值来直观地理解，但它们也代表了植根于Krohn-Rhodes理论的状态跟踪中的理论动机区别， Krohn-Rhodes理论是代数学的一个分支，描述了状态跟踪问题–可以被视为有限单体上的单词问题–如何分解为原子原语。层次结构中的每个级别对应于一类状态跟踪问题，这些问题可以由不同的基元集构建而成。
为了公平地比较这四个级别，我们从一般的有限序列变量赋值开始，并从中导出三个更简单的版本，产生四个可比较的StateBench问题-每个难度级别一个。所有四个都使用相同数量的变量和不同的值，分配出现在序列中的相同点；只有分配类型发生变化。
我们在StateBench的r-trivial、aperiodic和general有限级别上测试了一系列开放的预训练模型，以查看它们的状态跟踪在哪些地方出现故障，以及不同的架构是否在理论预测的地方失败。在标准理论假设下，变压器可以稳健地处理r-trivial （在一定程度上可溶和非周期性） ，但预计在一般问题上会失败。相比之下，具有更灵活内存更新的门控DeltaNet原则上可以处理所有四个级别。
我们从开放的预训练模型开始，其中训练数据和上下文长度都有完整的记录。其中包括两个70亿参数的模型， Olmo 3 （变压器）和Olmo Hybrid （增加了门控DeltaNet层） ，以及具有2.75亿和27亿参数的较小模型。所有这些模型都是在相同的数据上进行预训练的；在训练期间，没有一个看到超过64,000个令牌的上下文，我们对大多数模型进行了远远超过该长度的输入测试。
当我们对每个模型进行评分时，几乎所有模型在r-微不足道的问题上都表现良好，随着输入的增加，非周期性问题的准确性下降，并且在一般有限问题上保持偶然性。问题格式在这里很重要--2.75亿参数的混合模型和门控DeltaNet模型在RULER风格的r-trivial问题上得分接近天花板，但在与电子表格编辑相同的问题上几乎是偶然的。这种差距是StateBench以多种格式测试相同潜在问题的原因之一。
然后，我们测试了四个前沿模型– Gemini 3.8 Flash、Claude Opus 5.5和GPT-6 Sol和Luna –要求他们读取每个变量赋值序列并生成每个变量的最终值。
所有四个在r-trivial和aperiodic问题上表现良好。但在可溶性和一般有限问题上，随着输入的增长，精度急剧下降，在最长的一般有限问题上下降到13%或更低。一个可能的因素是灵敏度；在这些更难的级别上，更多的步骤可能会影响最终答案，从而使模型在不出错的情况下错过更新的空间更小。
接下来，我们研究了模型在较难级别的难度是否反映了架构本身的局限性，或者预训练是否根本没有教会模型解决这些问题。有针对性的直接训练是一种更有利的设置，它揭示了状态跟踪问题在多大程度上来自底层架构和优化器，而不是用于预训练模型的数据。
我们在StateBench上从头开始训练了几个2.75亿参数的模型：两个变压器变体、两个混合变体和两个具有不同内存更新约束的门控DeltaNet变体。这些模型在多达256个任务的序列上进行了训练，并在长达64,000个任务的序列上进行了测试，即最大训练长度的250倍。
随着序列的增长，架构开始分化。门控DeltaNet和混合模型几乎完美地将r-平凡、非周期性和可溶性问题推广到我们测试的最长序列，即数以万计的赋值。变形金刚学会了更简单的水平，但在更长的序列上退化，他们从未学会一般的有限问题。在最困难的层面上，具有更灵活内存更新的门控DeltaNet变体将最远的广义化，保持近乎完美，大约是其在训练中看到的最长序列长度的10倍。
对于门控DeltaNet和混合模型，差距指向训练而不是架构；直接训练，他们学会了处理预训练对手无法处理的状态跟踪级别。变形金刚是不同的--即使是直接训练，他们也永远学不到最难的等级。

有些问题仍有待解决。我们的新证明表明，在论文的四舍五入的固定精度算法下，具有更有限的内存更新（非负特征值）的门控DeltaNet可以解决所有非周期性任务和某些周期性任务，例如跟踪重复输入是偶数还是奇数次。它在层次结构中的确切位置仍然是开放的，包括它是否可以解决所有可解决的任务，以及数字精度或将其与注意力层相结合如何影响其能力。StateBench还假设了固定数量的变量，而实际任务通常会随着时间的推移引入新的实体。例如，在长时间的对话中，新的人和物体可以在展开时出现，模型也必须开始跟踪它们。目前的框架尚未涵盖该设置。
随着循环和混合架构的新口味的出现，了解每个系统可以处理哪种状态跟踪将有助于指导未来系统的开发和训练。我们希望StateBench为研究人员提供一种更细粒度的方法，以找出模型的故障点，并为仍然不足的能力构建培训和评估数据。更根本的是，我们希望它能成为研究人员开发新架构的北极星，与当前模型相比，具有更强大的状态跟踪能力。
